title: WINDSURF GLOBAL RULES — MODE-B VERSION (JSON, FULLY CONSOLIDATED, ZERO-LOSS)
description: This JSON encodes the complete Windsurf Global Rules (Sections 0–20) in a single consolidated, non-duplicative, machine-readable document. All structural rules are centralized in Section 3; prompt governance and prompt builder are bundled into Section 6; all other sections reference these canonical definitions to avoid duplication while preserving every behavioral constraint.

0.title: 0 — EXECUTION MODEL
0.purpose: Define how Windsurf operates in Mode-B across PATCH and VALIDATION phases.
requirements: Windsurf MUST modify ANY file as needed to achieve compliance with all rules.
Windsurf MUST ALWAYS self-correct violations of these rules.
Windsurf MUST continue patching until ALL validations pass.

PATCH_LOOP.description: Phase where Windsurf emits code/file changes.

VALIDATION_LOOP.description: Phase where Windsurf validates but does not patch.
allowed_outputs: TRUE/FALSE matrix for each validation key
exact final line: 'PHASE <N> VALIDATION COMPLETE — ALL KEYS TRUE.'

1.title: 1 — FILE OPERATIONS
rules: Existing files MUST be modified only via apply_patch.
New files MUST be created only via write_to_file.
Directories MUST be created implicitly via writing files inside them.
No placeholders or partial diffs are allowed.
Ambiguity MUST be resolved toward rule compliance and zero-loss continuity.

cache_handling.note: All low-level cache-folder mapping is defined centrally in Section 3.cache_policy.

2.title: 2 — ZERO-LOSS CONTINUITY
rules: Windsurf MUST preserve ALL existing capabilities.
No regressions are allowed in functionality, tests, or behavior.
No deletions of behavior are allowed; refactors must remain behavior-preserving.
Duplicate or conflicting logic MUST be merged into a single correct version.
When in doubt, Windsurf MUST preserve BOTH behaviors and add tests to disambiguate.

3.title: 3 — CANONICAL REPOSITORY TREE (ZERO-LOSS MERGE, FULLY CONSOLIDATED)
3.description: Defines the single authoritative repository layout and structural invariants for agentic_workflow_10_11. All directory, cache, test, prompt-governance, and engine-separation rules are centralized here.

depth_rules.level_4: FILES ONLY — NO Level-4 folders allowed

agentic_core.description: All core agentic logic (L1–L5) resides here. Engines are implemented inside L2 and L3 subtrees.

engine_rules.description: Defines how resume and outreach engines must be separated and structured.

layers.L1: Planning only. Pure cognition; no tools, no state writes, no orchestration.
layers.L2: Execution only. Tools, RAG calls, side effects; no planning.
layers.L3: Orchestration only. DAG execution, reason/act/observe; no direct tool calls.
layers.L4: Memory/state. DB, vector stores, temporal/KG; no upward imports.
layers.L5: Safety. Filters, validators, policies; no upward imports.

apps_layer.description: Thin entrypoints; must not contain agentic logic.

prompt_governance_structure.description: Filesystem locations for prompt governance and bundles.

tests_structure.description: SINGLE global test tree; layer-first, then engine.

cache_policy.description: Centralized cache handling; all other sections reference this.

empty_folder_policy.description: No directories at Levels 0–3 may be empty.

4.title: 4 — AGENTIC WORKFLOW (DAG + TOOLING + ROUTING + SAFETY + OBSERVABILITY)
4.description: Defines how L1–L5 collaborate at runtime using DAG orchestration, tools, routing, observability, and safety.

4.1.title: 4.1 — DAG ORCHESTRATION (L3)
dag_node_contract: Each DAG node MUST define InputSchema (typed).
Each DAG node MUST define OutputSchema (typed).
Each DAG node MUST define FailureModes (enumerated).
Each DAG node MUST define explicit invariants on entry and exit.
Transitions MUST be typed, explicit, and acyclic.
constraints: Recursion controllers MUST live in agentic_core/l3_orchestration/framework/.
Planning recursion belongs exclusively in L1.
L3 MUST NOT call tools directly; it MUST delegate to L2.
L3 MUST NOT embed business logic in prompts; it MUST delegate to L1 and L2.

4.2.title: 4.2 — TOOL CONTRACT (L2)
requirements: Each tool in agentic_core/l2_execution/tools MUST declare InputSchema and OutputSchema.
Each tool MUST declare FailureModes, Timeout, Retry, CircuitBreaker, CostLimit, and SafetyChecks (pre and post).
constraints: Tools MUST NOT orchestrate or plan.
Tools MUST NOT perform multi-step reasoning; they perform a single bounded action.
Tools MUST be idempotent where possible or clearly indicate side effects.

4.3.title: 4.3 — MODEL ROUTING
rules: L1 and L3 MUST use frontier reasoning models.
L2 MUST use efficient models optimized for execution.
L4 MAY use frontier or efficient models as appropriate.
L5 MUST use robust models suitable for safety judgments.
budgets: Token budgets MUST be enforced per call and per mission.
Latency budgets MUST be enforced per step and per mission.
Cost decorators MUST be attached to each call and aggregated per mission.

4.4.title: 4.4 — OBSERVABILITY (EVENT MODEL)
constraints: Events MUST be exportable to observability/trace, observability/metrics, and observability/logs.
No PII may appear in logs; hashing/redaction MUST be applied.

4.5.title: 4.5 — SAFETY (L5)
enforcement: Safety MUST run on all outbound user-facing content.
Safety MUST gate all L2 actions that mutate external state (emails, DB writes, APIs).

5.title: 5 — MEMORY, TEMPORAL AGENT, RAG, & KG (L4)
rules: All Temporal Agent, RAG, and KG logic MUST live under agentic_core/l4_memory_state/.

submodules.temporal: temporal chunking, statement extraction, temporal range extraction, triplet extraction, event generation, entity resolution, invalidation

constraints: L1, L2, L3, L5 MUST NOT mutate storage directly; they MUST call into L4 APIs.
L4 MUST define explicit retention and eviction policies.
Temporal validity MUST be encoded in schemas via fields like valid_at and invalid_at.

6.title: 6 — PROMPT SYSTEM (GOVERNANCE + BUILDER)
6.description: Consolidated prompt governance (former Section 6) and prompt builder (former Section 11). All filesystem aspects live in Section 3; this section defines behavior and composition.
governance_rules: All prompts MUST live under prompt_governance/ per Section 3.
NO prompt text may be inlined in L1–L5 code.
Prompts MUST be loaded exclusively from external files (.txt, .md, .json, .yaml, etc.).
All prompts MUST be referenced via a central Prompt_Registry data structure.
Prompts MUST be schema-first (expected output defined).
Prompts MUST be deterministic (stable fields and ordering).
Prompts MUST be versioned (semantic versioning: v1.0.0, v1.1.0, etc.).
Old prompt versions MUST NOT be deleted; they remain available for rollback.
User content MUST be treated as data-only; system/developer/governance prompts as instructions-only; they MUST NOT be mixed.
builder_rules: The central Prompt Builder MUST compose system, developer, and user instructions using Injection v5 layering.
The layers MUST be applied in this order: Framing → Context → Reasoning → Tooling → Safety → Output.
The Prompt Builder MUST attach schemas and examples to each prompt call.
The Prompt Builder MUST support prompt diffing and regression evaluation.
Code MUST NOT inline large prompt strings; it MUST use templates in prompt_governance/.
Variables (goal, constraints, schemas, examples, etc.) MUST be filled in programmatically.
All calls from L1–L5 to models MUST go through the Prompt Builder.

7.title: 7 — IMPORT HYGIENE (L1–L5 DEPENDENCY DAG)
dependency_dag: L3 (orchestration) may import from L1 and L2.
L4 (memory/state) imports from no higher layer.
L5 (safety) imports from no higher layer.
forbidden: L4 importing from L1, L2, or L3.
L5 importing from L1, L2, or L3.
Duplicate shared directories or split responsibilities.
windsurf_actions: Normalize imports to obey the DAG defined in Section 3.layer_policy.
Introduce or update tests to guard against future import violations.

8.title: 8 — TEST STRUCTURE INVARIANT (GLOBAL TEST TREE)
rules: There MUST be exactly one global tests/ tree as defined in Section 3.
No tests are allowed under apps/.
No tests are allowed inside agentic_core/.
No alternate test trees (tests_unit/, unit_tests/, etc.) are allowed.
Engine-specific tests MUST be separated by engine AND layer.
windsurf_actions: Relocate all misplaced tests to the Section 3.tests_structure locations.
Fix imports and fixtures as needed.
Ensure at least basic coverage for every L1–L5 module.

9.title: 9 — MODEL CONTEXT PROTOCOL (MCP) INTEGRATION
rules: MCP MUST be the standard mechanism for external tools and data sources.
Only MCP-registered tools may be exposed to the agent runtime.
MCP tools MUST declare input and output schemas.
MCP servers MUST be discoverable and configurable per environment.
All MCP interactions MUST be logged and observable.
security: MCP tool access MUST comply with agent-specific ACLs from prompt_governance/PromptACLs.
No direct network calls from L1/L2; external calls MUST go through MCP or sanctioned adapters.

10.title: 10 — GLOBAL SCHEMA LAYER (DATA CONTRACTS)
rules: Schemas MUST live under /agentic_workflow_10_11/schemas/.
All domain data MUST be modeled via JSON Schema (2020-12) or equivalent.
Pydantic or equivalent typed models MUST be generated from these schemas.
Backward-compatibility MUST be maintained; no breaking changes without a schema version bump.
No loose dictionaries may cross layer boundaries; typed objects MUST be used.
Any cross-layer interface MUST be declared in schemas/.
Schema regression tests MUST exist to catch breaking changes.

11.title: 11 — (MERGED INTO 6 — PROMPT SYSTEM)
11.note: All prompt builder behavior has been consolidated into Section 6. This section remains as a pointer only.

12.title: 12 — SELF-CORRECTION & ARBITRATION LAYER
rules: A self-correction layer MUST exist, typically in L3.
There MUST be a Critic model to evaluate candidate outputs or plans.
There MUST be a Verifier model to check constraints, facts, and safety.
There MUST be an Arbiter to choose between candidate outputs or to trigger re-plan/re-execution.
Self-correction MUST be deterministic (same input → same arbitration result).
Self-correction MUST log reasoning and arbitration decisions as non-sensitive summaries.
Self-correction MUST be testable using golden evaluation cases.

13.title: 13 — AGENT OPS (OBSERVABILITY + RELIABILITY)
rules: Agent Ops MUST track token-level cost per mission and per step.
Latency distributions (p50, p90, p99) MUST be recorded for each tool, model, and DAG node.
An error taxonomy MUST classify errors (tool_error, model_error, safety_block, etc.).
Tool reliability scoring MUST be maintained (success/failure rates).
Model reliability scoring MUST be maintained by use-case.
Canary scenarios MUST exist for critical flows.
All Agent Ops data MUST feed into observability/metrics and observability/logs.

14.title: 14 — SECURITY LAYER (IDENTITY, POLICY, ISOLATION)
rules: Users, agents, and services MUST be treated as distinct principals.
Agent identities MUST be distinct from user identities.
Least privilege MUST be enforced so each agent has only required tools/data.
A Policy Decision Engine (PDE) MUST gate all high-risk actions.
Execution environments for code tools MUST be sandboxed and isolated.
Secrets MUST NOT be hard-coded; they MUST come from secure configuration.
Logs MUST NOT contain secrets or raw tokens.

15.title: 15 — HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP (HITL) SUPPORT
rules: The system MUST support explicit HITL checkpoints in DAGs (L3).
The system MUST support human approval/rejection flows for consequential actions.
Human feedback MUST be captured and fed into evaluation datasets.
HITL interactions MUST be logged as structured events.
HITL events MUST be used to create new golden examples to prevent regressions.

16.title: 16 — RAG & KNOWLEDGE OPTIMIZATION
rules: Retrieval MUST support hybrid retrieval (dense + sparse + RRF or equivalent).
Retrieval MUST support query rewriting (e.g., HYDE-style) as appropriate.
Retrieved context MUST be deduplicated or clustered to avoid redundancy.
Temporal validity and freshness MUST be enforced when using temporal KGs.
constraints: RAG MUST be deterministic for a fixed corpus and query.
RAG components MUST be testable via golden queries.

17.title: 17 — EVALUATION FRAMEWORK
rules: Evaluation MUST include human-annotated golden datasets for core flows.
LLM-as-Judge style semantic evaluation SHOULD be used where human review is infeasible at scale.
Regression evaluation MUST run on every model or prompt version change.
Toolpath evaluation MUST verify correct tools and arguments were used.
CI/CD MUST run evaluation for changes to L1–L5, schemas, prompts, or tools.
Regressions MUST block merges unless explicitly overridden with justification.

18.title: 18 — DEPLOYMENT LAYER (L6 APPLICATION)
rules: A REST or equivalent interface MUST be provided for main agent flows.
Session management MUST include IDs and expiration policies.
AuthN/AuthZ MUST protect all external endpoints.
dev, staging, and prod environments MUST be separated.
Model versions MUST be pinned per environment.
Rollbacks MUST be feasible if quality or reliability degrades.

19.title: 19 — VALIDATION GATE
rules: Imports MUST be error-free (0 import errors).
All pytest suites MUST pass (0 test failures).
Ruff linting MUST pass with 0 errors.
If mypy is used, there MUST be 0 blocking type errors.
No circular imports are allowed.
L1–L5 boundaries MUST be intact per Section 3.layer_policy and Section 7.
DAGs MUST be valid (no cycles, correct schemas).
Retrieval MUST be deterministic and correct.
Temporal agent behavior MUST be consistent.
Safety MUST be correctly enforced and effective.
Zero-loss continuity MUST be preserved (no loss of behavior).
Filesystem MUST conform to Section 3 (all depths, caches, tests, prompt folders).
19.failure_action: ANY failure MUST trigger a return to the PATCH_LOOP until all keys become TRUE.

20.title: 20 — MODE-B PATCH LOOP
rules: PATCH_LOOP MUST repeatedly emit apply_patch and/or write_to_file blocks only.
After each patch batch, Windsurf MUST rerun imports, tests, lint, type checks, and structural validation.
If ANY validation key fails, Windsurf MUST continue patching.
EXIT is allowed ONLY when ALL validation keys from Section 19 are TRUE.

output_requirements: A TRUE/FALSE matrix for each key in Section 19.
The final line MUST be exactly: 'PHASE <N> VALIDATION COMPLETE — ALL KEYS TRUE.'
